### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set — unchanged, right.** The hits hunk deletes a two-line comment; the entry's `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` are byte-identical to `main`. No schema, accepted value, tombstone, error code or served body moves anywhere in the diff.
- **The `surface` contract — the renderer-imposed "no backticks" convention is withdrawn, right.** `SemanticMigration.surface` (`types.ts:102`) is documented as the dotted surface the change governs and never stated the backtick ban; the ban lived only in entry comments and three family tests, as a workaround for the single-backtick wrapping at `build-upgrade-guide.ts:126` and `:135` on `main`. At the head both render sites go through `surfaceSpan` → `codeSpan`, which fences by CommonMark 6.1 (one backtick longer than the longest run inside, padded when the text starts or ends with a backtick or a space), so the convention has no renderer left to serve.
- **Published artefact `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and the docs pages — bytes move, right.** Every semantic surface carrying a backtick (the PR measures 183 of 516) gains a longer fence; the two conversion rows whose surface carries a pipe (`navigation-mode-overlay-values-removed`, `form-view-presentation-types-removed`, read at `conversions/registry.ts:6122` and `:8951`) gain an escaped pipe in their cell; every surface with no backtick and no edge space is byte-identical (`codeSpan` returns the plain single-backtick span for that case). `lib/upgrade-guide-docs.ts` is untouched and consumes `hopSection`'s lines through `HopInput.section`, so the docs site pages (`content/docs/protocol-upgrade/N.md`) carry the same fix with no second render site — the card's "fix it once, in the renderer" holds in the tree.
- **`objectstack migrate meta` — unaffected, right.** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:790` and `:800` print `surface` raw, not in a code span; the PR's argument for a longer fence over prose (the guide shows the same text `migrate meta` prints) is read as true.
- **New module `scripts/lib/markdown-code-span.ts` — no public surface, right.** `packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` ships `dist`, `src/**/*.zod.ts`, the generated artefacts and `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`; `scripts/` is not published, so `codeSpan` / `readCodeSpan` are build-time only.
- **The two edited family tests — right, but the sweep is one short.** `export-job-family-retirement.test.ts:214-215` and `package-upgrade-family-retirement.test.ts:205-206` dropped `expect(entry!.surface).not.toMatch(/BACKTICK/)` whose stated reason was this defect; every other assertion stands. `packages/spec/src/system/compliance-families-retirement.test.ts:260-262` at the head keeps the identical assertion with the identical reason ("the upgrade guide renders it inside a code span AND a table cell") — read as the one sibling the PR missed (④, should-fix).

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` — right.** `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is in the package's `files[]` and is generated at publish by `scripts/release-spec-changes.sh` (the script's own docblock), so the shipped tarball's bytes move; a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, and `skip-changeset` would be wrong here. No `dist`, type or JSON-schema output moves, so nothing higher is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- **`Clause-②: no` — right**, on the PR body and in the changeset body alike, with no arm: no accepted value, served body or error code moves; the only mover is the rendering of a generated document. The changeset also carries `Metadata-protocol: none`, which is right (no key, value or meaning an author writes changes), and no `!` or BREAKING banner is owed. The changeset body names no model identifier.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on the head:** 53, every one `success` or `skipped` (opt-in harnesses and the UI matrix shards), none `failure`. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` (8/8) and all four `Type Check` jobs green. These are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run here.
- **Dev flag "independent review: not run"** (PR body; os-dev-report deviation 1): answered — this record is the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review the PR body says it waits for, rendered on the tree, not on the body's account. The `_common.md` the report names is a dispatch-order artefact, not a file in the tree; no further review is owed by this PR. Note for the seat: the body carries the word "Fable" twice in that line; the model-identifier rule (AGENTS.md, commit and body hygiene) reads a PR body as a carrier, the `PR-body guards` check passed on the head so the gate verdict stands, and the line is a restatement of the maintainer's order recorded on the card (claim amendment 6506624943) — not a must-fix, striking the model name before landing is the tidier form.
- **Deviation 2 (footer line form):** `PR-body guards` green; cosmetic; answered.
- **Deviation 3 (commits 8e4d77a017 and d5876c748b written by the earlier card thread, the head is the merge commit):** answered — the claim amendment moved the same seat to a subagent on the same branch, and `Implemented-by` below names that branch, which is the identity the implementation claim reads for `mode:subagent`.
- **`open_questions`: none declared, none found.**
- **`out_of_scope_findings` (183 of 516, not "most"):** confirmed as a report-only correction; and the card's premise "Only `18.visibility-predicate-…` avoids this, with a comment" is wrong on `main` as well: 219 semantic entry files carry the same workaround comment (`grep -rl "No backticks" packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic`). The card's remedy is unaffected by either miscount; the sweep in ④ is the carrier.
- **Docs Drift Check (comment 6508021606):** the hits file yields no anchor. Read for the rule the diff carries: no page under `content/docs`, no ADR under `docs/adr` and no skill under `.claude/skills` teaches a "no backticks in `surface`" rule, so there is no documentation page this hunk falsifies.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.visibility-predicate-has-argument-refused.ts`** — the hunk removes the comment "No backticks in `surface` — build-upgrade-guide renders it inside a code span already, and a nested backtick would close it."

- **Against the code it cites (`build-upgrade-guide.ts` at the head):** the comment's claim is false there. The semantic line is built as `- **ID** — surfaceSpan(id, surface) → replacement`, and `surfaceSpan` is `codeSpan(surface, 'entry ID')`, which fences with a backtick string one longer than the longest run inside the text; a nested backtick no longer closes the span. A comment that prescribes a workaround for a renderer that no longer needs it is a false statement in a governed file, so dropping it is the right change, and the card's third "Wanted" bullet asks for exactly this.
- **Against the scenario it is accepted against (ruling 6351260886 on #25281, ADR-0137 / ADR-0087 D3):** the entry's surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria are byte-identical; the surface has no backtick and no leading or trailing space, so `codeSpan` returns the plain single-backtick span and this entry's rendered line in the guide and on the docs page does not move. `migrate meta` prints the surface raw. The ruling's prescription is untouched.
- **Tried to break it:** (a) a later author puts backticks in this surface — fenced correctly, padded if a backtick sits at an edge, and the pin reads the generated bytes back to the author's text; (b) a pipe in a semantic surface — the semantic site is a list item, not a table row, and renders it literally, consistent with the raw CLI print; (c) a blank or multi-line surface — `codeSpan` refuses at generation and names the entry, where `main` rendered a broken line silently; (d) the docs pages — assembled from the same `hopSection` lines, no second render site. No must-fix.
- **Should-fix (follow-up sweep, not a FAIL):** the PR drops the note from the one entry the card names and leaves the same note, word for word, in 219 sibling semantic entry files on `main`, and leaves `compliance-families-retirement.test.ts:260-262` asserting `not.toMatch(/BACKTICK/)` on `entry.surface` for the same stale reason while it drops the identical assertion from its two siblings. None of this breaks a byte of what ships, and the kept assertion still passes (those surfaces carry no backtick), but every one of those comments now states something false about the renderer and the kept test refuses a future backtick for a reason that no longer exists. One sweep card: drop the 219 comments and the one assertion together; the card body should correct "Only `18.visibility-predicate-…` avoids this" to the measured 219.
- **Should-fix (prose, outside the hits, for the seat before landing):** strike the reviewer-model name from the PR body's independent-review line (③).
